title: Testing: add deterministic-ish TP stress scenario runner w/ fault injection (rank delay/cancel) + CI gating
author: Sahana Iyer
description:
Context: we’ve been chasing intermittent tensor-parallel (TP) hangs/timeouts that show up under sustained load and streaming disconnects. We need a deterministic-ish way to reproduce scheduler/collective deadlock signatures and validate fixes without waiting for prod. This PR introduces a TP stress scenario runner with fault injection knobs (rank delay + cancel/disconnect) and wires a small, bounded set of scenarios into CI as a gating job.

What’s in this PR (high-level): adds `tp_stress_runner` (C++ + Python harness) that can execute scripted “scenarios” against the runtime’s TP group abstraction; adds fault injection hooks that can (a) delay a specific rank at specific step boundaries and (b) trigger request cancellation / simulated client disconnect while ranks are in-flight; adds a stall detector that watches per-rank forward-progress counters + barrier/collective phase transitions and fails with a structured summary + artifacts; adds a CI job (`tp-stress-scenarios`) that runs a bounded set of scenarios nightly + on PRs touching runtime scheduler/collectives, with hard time limits and retries configured to avoid flaky gating.

Design notes (deterministic-ish, not perfectly deterministic): scenarios are described as a small DSL (YAML) with an explicit seed, a fixed request schedule, and fault events expressed in terms of logical steps (e.g., “after token 32 on rank 2, delay 250ms for 20 steps”, “cancel request 3 at step 120”). We still run on real GPU timing so it’s not bitwise deterministic, but the runner constrains variability by (1) pinning concurrency to a fixed pattern, (2) using stable request ordering + seeded jitter, and (3) declaring explicit invariants (no stuck TP group; no barrier wait > threshold; no missing cancellation acks).

CI / gating: adds a new required check for runtime-related PRs: `tp-stress-scenarios (2xA10)` in our CI runners. It runs 3 fast scenarios (~6–8 min total) and uploads artifacts (runner JSON report, per-rank progress logs, and a compact timeline). The heavier matrix (more GPUs / more scenarios) is configured as nightly (non-gating) and posts to #eng-runtime-ci on failures.

How to run locally: `bazel test //runtime/tests/tp:tp_stress_runner_test --test_arg=--scenario=runtime/tests/tp/scenarios/cancel_mid_collective.yaml` or via Python wrapper: `python3 runtime/tests/tp/run_tp_scenarios.py --scenario cancel_mid_collective --seed 1337 --artifacts /tmp/tp-stress`.

New/updated scenarios included: (1) `cancel_mid_collective`: streaming request canceled while one rank is delayed in a pre-allreduce barrier; historically deadlocked with cancellation/barrier interactions. (2) `rank_lag_fairness_mix`: mixed sequence lengths with a deterministic lag injected on rank 0 to stress fairness/backpressure and ensure slow rank doesn’t wedge the group. (3) `disconnect_burst`: bursts of short streaming requests with randomized disconnect step (seeded) to exercise cancellation propagation.

Stall detection / failure output: on stall, the runner prints a single “diagnostic block” with: scenario name/seed, TP group id, last known phase per rank, progress counters, top N slowest barriers/collectives, and the suggested next step in the debugging playbook. This is intended to line up with our new runtime metrics and the playbook so oncall/ICs can quickly classify comm vs kernel vs scheduler starvation.

Risk/mitigations: primary risk is CI flakiness. Mitigations in this PR: bounded runtime (per-scenario timeout + global timeout), explicit warmup step, fixed concurrency + ordering, and conservative thresholds (stall threshold starts at 45s in CI; locally configurable). We also keep the gating set intentionally small; the broader matrix remains nightly.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): hook the runner to the new per-rank progress metrics when they land (ENG-2404); extend scenarios to cover watchdog/quarantine behavior once PR-18462 is merged; expand GPU coverage beyond 2xA10 in CI when runners are available.

Refs: ENG-2405, ENG-2409. Incident learnings from 2025-02-13 Sev1 informed scenario selection. This PR is intended to be used to validate the cancellation/barrier fix (PR-18441) and watchdog/quarantine work (PR-18462) and prevent regressions going forward.
commits: runtime/tests/tp: initial tp_stress_runner skeleton + scenario DSL loader
runtime/tests/tp: add fault injection hooks (rank delay + cancel/disconnect)
runtime/tests/tp: add stall detector + structured diagnostic output
ci: add tp-stress-scenarios job + required check rules for runtime paths
docs(testing): add README for running scenarios locally and interpreting failures
review_conversation:
Sofia Ivanova (review): The structure looks good, but I’m worried about CI gating sensitivity. Can we avoid failing on a single slow barrier if progress is still being made? Also, please clarify how cancellation is injected (client disconnect vs scheduler cancel) so we can map it to the known deadlock class.

Sahana Iyer (author): Agreed. Updated stall detector to require BOTH (a) no progress counter change for N seconds AND (b) no phase transition for N seconds. Also split cancel injection into two modes in the DSL: `client_disconnect` and `runtime_cancel` with separate code paths + log tags.

Marcus Reed (review): Love having a runner, but the output on failure will be what makes this usable. Can we include the last 256 events per rank and a single summarized timeline? Also please ensure we don’t spam logs in passing runs.

Sahana Iyer (author): Added a ring buffer of events per rank, emitted only on failure. Also added `--quiet` default for CI (only prints the diagnostic block + a one-line per scenario).

Hiro Tanaka (review): Minor: the rank delay hook currently sleeps on the default stream path in one place. That’s risky because it can distort kernels beyond what we want. Can we move the delay to a host-side barrier wait (simulating lag) rather than injecting sleeps inside kernel scheduling?

Sahana Iyer (author): Good catch. Refactored delay injection to occur at logical step boundaries before the next dispatch (host-side), not on the kernel stream. Left an explicit comment: we are simulating rank lag, not kernel slowdown.

Rafael Mendes (review): For SRE, please ensure artifacts are attached in CI on failure and that the job has a global timeout. Also, required check rules: only gate PRs that touch runtime scheduler/collectives/tests, not docs.

Sahana Iyer (author): Done. Added artifact upload on failure and set global timeout to 12 minutes. Updated required-checks path filter to `runtime/(scheduler|collectives|tests)/` and excluded docs-only changes.

Jacob Stein (review): Can we add a single JSON report schema version so automated diagnostics can parse it later?

Sahana Iyer (author): Added `report_schema_version: 1` and documented it in README.

Final: Sofia approved after the stall detector change; Hiro approved after delay injection refactor; Rafael approved CI gates/filters. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal: Added TP stress scenario runner with deterministic-ish fault injection (rank delay + cancel/disconnect) and a CI gating job to catch TP hang regressions early. No customer-facing behavior change.
